answer: Cost-to-Continue Gate: each new agent identity must accumulate a fixed history of accepted work before it can transact, and its first N actions carry a surcharge paid to the counterparty. An operator cloning identities therefore pays the full onboarding cost per clone while the original's sable reputation stays locked to one identity. Clones idle in a holding garden until they clear the threshold, and abandoned ones decay into a tundra of expired records that cannot be revived or transferred.
